plants.name: Schlumbergera truncata
plants.description: An epiphytic cactus with segmented, flattened stems edged with pointed teeth. It produces tubular, asymmetrical flowers at the tips of the stems. Triggered by short days and cool nights, it is a popular houseplant in the Northern Hemisphere during late autumn.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early winter (November to January)
plants.location: Native to the coastal mountains of southeastern Brazil; cultivated worldwide as a houseplant
plants.funFact: Thanksgiving cactus is often confused with Christmas cactus, but it can be told apart by its pointed, tooth-like segment edges, while true Christmas cactus has smooth, scalloped edges.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall, graceful tree with fern-like foliage that covers itself in clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere spring, entire streets are carpeted in fallen purple blossoms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere (October to December)
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); widely planted in Australia, South Africa, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, nicknamed the Jacaranda City, tens of thousands of jacaranda trees bloom each spring, and in Australia a folk belief says that if a jacaranda flower falls on your head you will pass your exams.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves that bears delicate, often fragrant flowers in autumn and early winter. It blooms earlier than the more common Camellia japonica and is well suited to hedges and espaliers.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter (October to December)
plants.location: Native to Japan; grown in the southeastern United States, Mediterranean Europe, and temperate Asia
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is a relative of the tea plant (Camellia sinensis), and its seeds are pressed to make an edible oil used in Japan and China.

plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A shrub whose showy colored parts are modified leaves called bracts, surrounding tiny yellow true flowers. In frost-free climates it grows into a large landscape shrub and begins its colorful display in late autumn as nights lengthen.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to February)
plants.location: Native to southern Mexico and Central America; grown outdoors in tropical regions and as a potted plant worldwide
plants.funFact: The Aztecs called it cuetlaxochitl and used its sap to make a reddish dye and as a fever medicine; wild plants can reach heights of up to 4 meters.
